sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Pseudotsuga menziesii, Douglas-fir, is a very large evergreen conifer of western North America. Mature trees vary with variety and site: Rocky Mountain trees commonly reach 30–37 m, while coast Douglas-fir on favorable sites can reach about 76 m.

sections.title: Needles and cones
sections.text: The flat needles are about 2–3.5 cm long. Hanging seed cones are about 4–9 cm long and have distinctive three-pointed bracts projecting beyond the scales.

sections.title: Uses
sections.text: The timber is widely used in construction. No human food use is established for the illustrated leaves or cones in the sources consulted.
